newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Slumbering Australia bonds end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Slumbering Australia bonds end slightly lower.

text.p: Australian bonds ended the week with a lacklustre performance which saw them trade in narrow ranges just under their previous closing levels.

While the fourth weaker close in U.S. Treasuries saw bonds open weaker, they found good support early on and remained bouyed in the first hour of trading by some optimistic expectations that the Reserve Bank would cut interest rates.

When there was no announcement forthcoming at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT), bonds softened a couple of points, and settled in for a quiet day's trading but remain well supported by widespread expectations of a November interest rate cut.
U.S. retail trade and producer price index data for September will be released later on Friday.
The Treasuries market reaction to them will set the tone for early trading next week, dealers said.
"There's nothing to say -- it's all on hold until tonight's numbers," one trader said of the market.

The main local event next week is the RBA's quarterly report on the economy, which will be scrutinised for any clues on the thinking of policy makers ahead of third quarter inflation and wages data on October 23 and 24, respectively, traders said.

Economists surveyed by Reuters expect underlying inflation to rise 0.6 percent in the third quarter, leading to a 2.5 percent annual rate. Wages are seen rising 1.0 percent in the quarter and 3.7 percent over the year, figures which economists said would be supportive of a November rate cut.

The bond spread to U.S. 10-years ends at 99 points, after being at 97 in early trade, its narrowest close in 2-1/2 years, traders said. NZ long end feels some pressure ahead of this weekend's elections
